newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE-100 to consolidate near term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE-100 to consolidate near term.

text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index is poised for a period of consolidation after Friday's dramatic 88 point fall and will try to probe resistance around 4,002 to 4,013 in the near term, technical analysts said on Monday.
By 1044 GMT, the FTSE 100 was up 30.1 points, or 0.76 percent, at 3993.1.

"The dramatic action on Friday broke the uptrend that's been in place since mid-summer," said Credit Suisse technical analyst David Sneddon. "The FTSE 100 broke key support at the early November low just below the 3,900 but it hasn't closed below there so that keeps the bullish options open."

Sneddown said the market would likely edge higher in the short term, targetting resistance between 4,002 and 4,013. "If it can break 4,013 there's no reason not to fill the top of the gap to 4033-4040," he added.
But he said the market would be under renewed pressure around these levels to fall and re-test the key November 11 low of 3,896. He said interim support would come in at 3,964 then 3,950.
Kirit Shah, technical analyst at Sanwa International, said Friday's stronger close meant the market could be in for a brief rally before slipping again.
"The big levels that are important are 4,000 then 4,025 to 4,030," said Shah. "The market will fall after that."
